A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlphaRL study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and plotted results. Existing material can be matched across appendix and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original rank-truncation experiments, analyses of training trajectories and reasoning behavior, and AlphaRL evaluations on six benchmarks, including Table 1 and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds model evaluations, self-play and transfer results, and on-policy distillation/DPO analyses in Tables 3–8 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The SVD-based Rank-1 reconstruction, norm rescaling, and single-component PLS prediction procedure remain unchanged in Sections 2.1 and 4.1. Applying AlphaRL to additional models and self-play does not introduce a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: v3 adds adversarial self-play on Kuhn Poker and reports using Simple Negotiation, plus MATH-500 evaluation after game training (Tables 5–6; Appendix B). It also adds Math-Step-DPO-10K preference training data. These substantially broaden training and task conditions beyond the retained reasoning benchmarks.

E2.justification: On-policy distillation and offline DPO are newly evaluated alongside offline distillation, SFT, and DAPO in the update-norm, rank-retention, and embedding comparisons (Tables 7–8; Figure 9). These add substantively different comparison methods for assessing whether the observed structure is specific to RL.

E3.justification: v3 adds a Qwen3-4B self-play protocol with roughly 200 checkpoints, saving every two epochs, and win-rate evaluation against a Gemini opponent. It also expands model configurations and evaluated training stages. The reported SFT mini-batch size changes from 8 to 4 and accumulation steps from 256 to 512; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New norm comparisons, rank-retention sweeps, and embedding plots examine low-rank behavior under on-policy distillation and DPO (Tables 7–8; Figure 9). Tables 3–6 additionally test robustness across model scales and initializations, adversarial training, and game-to-mathematics transfer. The original ablations and token-level analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds point estimates without introducing reported training seed/run counts, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests. The existing plotted bands and the main evaluation's averaging over 32 sampled responses remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original plotted results are retained, while Tables 3–8 add checkpoint/model scores, game and transfer outcomes, and new comparator diagnostics. For example, Table 5 reports 59% poker win rate at 40% training with AlphaRL versus 65% after full training. Table 8 adds Rank-1 entries of 56.40% for online distillation and 62.25% for DPO.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including the SVD reconstruction, trajectory definitions, and PLS/OLS formulation, are unchanged. The linear-projection appendix moves from D to E. Neither version supplies a theoretical proof of the empirical properties, and the stated lack of rigorous theoretical foundations remains.

C1.justification: The main contributions remain Rank-1 Dominance, Rank-1 Linear Dynamics, and AlphaRL acceleration. The abstract retains the over-99% recovery, up-to-2.5-times speedup, and over-96% performance claims. The introduction's expanded experimental inventory supplies additional support without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 Appendix C explicitly concludes that low-rank update structure is not unique to RL, citing the new on-policy distillation and DPO evidence. This materially qualifies v1's RL-specific interpretation, although broader RL-specific wording remains in the main text. Appendix A also interprets the new experiments as extending applicability across initializations and adversarial environments.

D1.justification: The setup appendix adds model/checkpoint and dataset mappings, the Llama cold-start procedure, and hardware coverage of 8 or 16 H800 GPUs instead of only 8. It revises the SFT settings and clarifies RL gradient accumulation. The advertised code/model location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository; actual accessibility is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for on-policy distillation, DPO, SPIRAL, AlphaZero, GLM, and Llama. Section 5 adds brief discussion of CISPO and Mukherjee et al.'s sparse-subnetwork findings. These extend the context without substantially reorganizing the paper's positioning around RL parameter dynamics.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Changes include local introduction and conclusion edits, expanded setup descriptions, a new Additional Experiment appendix preceding the renumbered appendices, acknowledgments, and updated authorship and publication headers.

P2.justification: Six added tables substantially expand the presentation of model trajectories, self-play/transfer results, and training-method diagnostics. New Figure 9 supplies paired embedding plots and shares a page with the relocated Figure 8. Existing figures are retained, with v1 Figures 9–28 becoming v3 Figures 10–29.

improvement.justification: The new self-play/transfer experiments and on-policy distillation/DPO controls improve assessment of applicability and qualify the earlier RL-specific explanation. However, this qualification is incompletely integrated into the main text, and new Tables 3–4 contain inconsistent averages: Table 4's DeepSeek 20%+AlphaRL row reports 48.23 although its six scores average about 68.23. The informative controls support a modest net improvement, while these reporting problems limit confidence in the expanded evidence.
